# quarry — agent guide

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
One CLI and skills over scientific resources, with domains as lenses
<!-- ops:identity end -->

## Setup

`just setup` links the sibling checkouts, then runs `uv sync --group dev` behind
work-link. quarry needs `refs` and `nodes` cloned beside this checkout. Run
`(cd ../refs && just registry-sync)` first to write the registry copies. `just link-siblings`
fails early when either is missing. Python 3.13 or later,
uv, and just are required. The checkout uses `.githooks/` via
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.

## Gates

- `just test-one <pytest args>` runs a path under `tests/`, `path::name`, or `-k expr` (protected; always runs under `.tt.toml`).
- `just test-fast` runs the whole small suite (`broad_targets`; skipped locally when `.tt.toml` sets `automatic_broad = false` unless `TT_FORCE=1`). Subprocess CLI
  tests prevent reliable testmon selection; keep the full suite until affected selection is justified.
- `just test` runs the full suite (`broad_targets`; skipped locally when `.tt.toml` sets `automatic_broad = false` unless `TT_FORCE=1`).
- `just test-full` forces the full offline suite (`TT_FORCE=1 just test`) even when `.tt.toml` disables automatic broad runs.
- `just ci-python` runs portable hygiene (`ops-check`, `ops-docs check`, `quarry check`) and the full pytest suite with JUnit XML evidence in `QUARRY_CI_EVIDENCE_DIR`.
- `just check-hygiene` (aliased as `just check`) runs `ops-check`, `ops-docs check`, `quarry check`, and `tasks check`.
- `just install` links `bin/quarry` into `~/.local/bin/quarry` (main checkout only; refuses from a worktree). It is a host change: run it once per host.
- `just live` probes every catalog route with its smallest real request and prints one line per route (`ok` or `failed`); it contacts the live services, reports without gating, and is never part of `just test`.

Use the just recipes so tools/tt records each run; never call pytest directly.

## Layout

- `src/quarry/`: the Python package.
- `src/quarry/catalog/`: resources and domains. The registry comes from refs.
- `src/quarry/adapters/`: one module per supported resource; `eutils.py` is shared by GEO and PubMed.
- `tests/`: tests; `tests/fixtures/` holds recorded resource responses.
- `tests/recordings/`: scenarios that `just record <resource>` captures.
- `tests/live.py`: one probe per catalog route, run by `just live`; a new route needs a probe (a test enforces it).
- `bin/quarry`: the launcher `just install` links into `~/.local/bin`.
- `skills/`: agent skills; the resource notes in them are generated by `quarry skills build`.
- `tools/`: timing and gate tools vendored from ops.

## Rules

Tests never reach the network: they replay `tests/fixtures/`, refreshed only by
`just record <resource>`. A live call in a test makes the suite depend on services
that fail (ENA's count endpoint returned 500 during the myeloma survey).

A new command or option is a row in ops `cli.toml` first, then `vendored adopt cli.toml`;
the conformance test fails on any difference.

Catalog owned prefixes must use the registry's canonical spelling. Local-prefix
declarations must be lowercase so validation and owner routing agree, and their patterns
must be in refs' pattern dialect (`[0-9]`, not `\d`). `quarry check` reports one that is not;
startup leaves it out of the registry, so every catalog-reading command other than `quarry check` refuses
with `catalog_invalid` and points at `quarry check`. A new external scheme that Bioregistry
lacks goes in refs' shared local schemes (registry/local-schemes.toml there), so a prefix has one grammar everywhere,
and the catalog lists it under `prefixes`; catalog `local_prefixes` stay supported, with
patterns in refs' dialect.

## Development

Add a resource TOML and its adapter under the catalog/package layout. Record
responses through `just record <resource>`, add a smallest probe in
`tests/live.py`, and use `uv run quarry skills build` to regenerate resource
notes. Handwritten skill guidance lives outside the marked regions.
The [CLI guide](docs/cli.md) covers workflows, the [JSON model](docs/output.md)
defines outputs, and the [literature guide](docs/literature.md) covers eligibility.

## Diagnosing checks

`quarry check --json` reports kind, where and detail for each finding.
Fix the input named by where, then rerun. Catalog-reading commands refuse
an invalid catalog and point to this check.

| Finding kinds | Repair |
| --- | --- |
| catalog_invalid | Repair TOML syntax, required fields, types, unknown keys or file/id mismatch. |
| unknown_role, unknown_route_kind, unknown_auth | Use catalog-supported role, route and auth values. |
| missing_key_env, missing_key_location | Declare the route's credential variable and query/header placement. |
| unknown_key_scheme, invalid_key_scheme | Use a supported key_scheme (`bearer`) only on an authenticated route with `key_env`, `key_header = "Authorization"` and no `key_param`. |
| missing_adapter, orphan_adapter | Make the resource's module importable and name every shipped adapter. |
| unknown_prefix, noncanonical_prefix | Use canonical registry spelling and lowercase local declarations. |
| local_pattern_unsupported | Express the pattern in refs' portable dialect. |
| local_prefix_in_bioregistry, prefix_owned_twice | Use registry prefixes without shadowing and give each prefix one owner. |
| pitfall_incomplete | Supply nonempty summary, handling and public evidence. |
| missing_resource, search_default_outside | List existing resource IDs and include default-search resources locally. |
| missing_domain, include_cycle | Correct includes and remove inclusion cycles. |
| unmapped_facet_namespace | Map the facet namespace to a known prefix. |

An ops-docs region mismatch needs `just docs`. Marker/type findings need
the authored reference corrected. A CLI-surface failure needs the live parser
and adopted table compared against the authoritative source. An ops-check
failure names the path or source-owned file to repair. Maintainer
`tasks check` requires registered task records and diagnoses their links.
Focused tests run through `just test-one`; fixture-based tests stay offline.
